summary: In Greek mythology, Leucippus (Ancient Greek: Λεύκιππος, "white horse") was a Messenian prince, a son of Perieres and Gorgophone and brother of Aphareus. He married Philodice and fathered three daughters: the two Leucippides, Phoebe and Hilaera, and Arsinoe, who bore Asclepius and Eriopis to Apollo. The Boeotian town of Leuctra was said to derive its name from him.

etymology: The name Leucippus (Ancient Greek: Λεύκιππος, romanized: Leúkippos) literally translates as "white horse."

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: In Greek mythology, Leucippus (Ancient Greek: Λεύκιππος, romanized: Leúkippos, lit. 'white horse') was a Messenian prince. The Boeotian town of Leuctra is said to have derived its name from him.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Leucippus was the son of Gorgophone and Perieres, and brother of Aphareus, amongst others. He was the father of three daughters, each borne by his wife Philodice, daughter of Inachus: two Leucippides (Phoebe and Hilaera), and Arsinoe, mother of Asclepius and Eriopis begotten by the god Apollo.

sections.heading: Mythology
paragraphs: It is said that Leucippus, together with his brother Aphareus, inherited their father's kingdom upon his death, but the latter kept the greater authority of the two. Castor and Polydeuces abducted and married Leucippus' daughters, Phoebe and Hilaera. In return, Idas and Lynceus, nephews of Leucippus and rival suitors, killed Castor. Polydeuces was granted immortality by Zeus, and further persuaded Zeus to share his gift with Castor.
